ing: frozen, thawed, or fresh; spinach works if unavailable
st: Blend or finely chop the cassava leaves with a splash of water into a coarse green paste.
Put the chicken, half the onion, garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt in a pot with [[4 cup]] water. Simmer 25 minutes.
Add the leaves and the whole chili. Cover and simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] palm oil, the smoked fish and [[2 tbsp]] peanut butter.
Cook uncovered on low for 40 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil rises to the top.
Fry the remaining onion in a little palm oil from the pot and stir it in for the last 5 minutes.
Check that the chicken is at least 165°F (74°C). Season with salt.
Cook the rice with [[3.5 cup]] water and serve the stew over it.
Wash and chop the leaves finely. Pound or pulse briefly in a blender with a splash of water.
Simmer the chicken with half the onion, garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt in [[3 cup]] water for 25 minutes.
Add the leaves and the chili and cook, covered, for 25 minutes.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] palm oil and the smoked fish.
Simmer uncovered 25 minutes until thick and the oil shines on top.
Cook the remaining onion in a bit of the oil for 4 minutes and stir in.
Check the chicken is 165°F (74°C) and season with salt.
Serve over rice cooked from [[2 cup]] rice and [[3.5 cup]] water.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot and brown the chicken for 8 minutes. Remove it.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the same pot for 4 minutes.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste for 1 minute.
Whisk [[0.75 cup]] peanut butter with [[1 cup]] hot water until smooth.
Pour it into the pot with [[3 cup]] more water. Add the chicken, chili and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Simmer on low, partly covered, for 40 minutes, stirring so it does not stick.
Check the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Skim the oil from the top if you like.
Serve over rice cooked from [[1.5 cup]] rice and [[2.5 cup]] water.
Blend the tomatoes, bell peppers, chili and 1 onion until smooth.
Season the chicken with salt, curry powder and thyme. Brown it in [[0.33 cup]] oil for 8 minutes per side and remove.
Cook the other onion in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste and fry 4 minutes.
Pour in the blended mix and simmer 20 minutes until reduced and oily.
Add [[3 cup]] broth, the bay leaves and [[1 tsp]] salt. Return the chicken. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the rinsed rice, cover tightly, and cook on low for 25 minutes without stirring.
Check the chicken is at least 165°F (74°C) and the rice is tender. Fluff and serve.
Simmer the beef in [[4 cup]] water with half the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt for 40 minutes until tender.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] palm oil in a second pot and cook the remaining onion, garlic and chili for 4 minutes.
Add the beef with its broth and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the sliced okra and cook 10 minutes, stirring, until the soup thickens.
Add the fish and cook gently 5 minutes until it is opaque.
Check the beef reaches at least 145°F (63°C), and season with salt.
Serve with rice cooked from [[1.5 cup]] rice and [[2.5 cup]] water.
Put the onion, ginger, garlic, tomatoes and chilies in a pot with [[5 cup]] water.
Add [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[0.25 tsp]] cloves, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend roughly if you like a thicker broth, or leave it clear.
Return to the pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and cook 8 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Squeeze in the lime juice and add salt to taste.
Serve in deep bowls while very hot.
Soak the peas in water for 4 hours, or overnight.
Rub the peas between your hands to loosen the skins, then rinse until the skins float away.
Blend the peas with the onion, chili, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt into a thick paste.
Whip the paste with a spoon for 2 minutes so it turns light and fluffy.
Heat [[2 cup]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Drop in rounded spoonfuls and fry in batches 3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Peel the plantains and slice them diagonally into pieces about 0.5 inch thick.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] chili powder.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the onion for 3 minutes until soft and lift it out.
Fry the plantains in one layer for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with the onion on top.
Toast the rice flour in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until lightly golden, stirring.
Grind the peanuts in a food processor into coarse crumbs, not paste.
Mix peanuts and toasted flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat [[0.75 cup]] sugar with [[0.25 cup]] water over medium heat for 5 minutes until syrupy and golden.
Take off the heat and stir in [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Pour the syrup over the peanut mix and stir quickly to coat it.
Press firmly into a lined 8-inch pan.
Cool for 20 minutes and cut into bars.
Grate the ginger finely, using a box grater.
Put the ginger, cloves and [[4 cup]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar until it dissolves, then remove from the heat.
Let it steep for 30 minutes.
Strain through a fine strainer into a pitcher. Add [[4 cup]] cold water and the juice of 3 limes.
Chill until cold and serve over ice.
